(2023). MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI.
creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
description: MMMU is a massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines and 30 subjects.
name: MMMU
rai:annotatorDemographics: 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step requires authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations are found. In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A user-friendly web interface developed for data annotation and verification.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given the arising data contamination concems of foundation models, the annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
rai:dataCollection: The questions in our benchmark were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Document analysis, Web Scraping
rai:dataLimitations: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications.
rai:dataSocialImpact: It is of both intellectual and societal importance to closely monitor the progress towards Expert AGI. The benchmark will prove instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI.
rai:dataUseCases: Evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.
